paths.description: Understand the Fingen application suite, module architecture, and core system concepts.

nodes.title: Platform Architecture
nodes.description: Overview of Fingen's multitier architecture and environment topology.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Fingen is a cloud hosted financial operations platform built on a microservices architecture across three isolated environments. Understanding the platform topology is the starting point for every L2 incident.

## Architecture Tiers
- **Presentation Layer**: React Web Portal and client facing REST API
- **Application Layer**: Five independently deployable microservices: Account Service (8001), Transaction Service (8002), Reporting Service (8003), Integration Gateway (8004), Config Service (8005)
- **Data Layer**: PostgreSQL primary database, Redis cache (session & dedup), S3-compatible blob storage

## Environments
- **Development**: Engineer workstations and CI pipelines; never holds real client data
- **UAT**: Preproduction validation; mirrors Production schema; used for change verification and client sign off
- **Production**: Live environment serving all clients; all changes require an approved Change Request (CR)

## Service Health Dashboard
The Operations Dashboard shows RED / AMBER / GREEN per service. AMBER = degraded but operational (error rate 1 to 5%). RED = down or error rate above SLA threshold (>5%). The status change timestamp is your incident start time.

## L2 Diagnostic Entry Point
When an incident is raised: (1) identify the affected service from the dashboard, (2) pull service logs for ERROR/CRITICAL entries in the incident window, (3) confirm whether the issue is isolated to one account or platform wide before escalating.
nodes.sample_question: Describe the three environments in Fingen and explain why each exists.
nodes.sample_answer: Development is used for active coding and unit testing. UAT is used to validate features before going live. Production serves live customers. Keeping them separate protects customer data and prevents untested code from reaching end users.
nodes.scenario_context: You are onboarding to the client account. A colleague asks you to test a new feature configuration before it goes live. Which environment should you use?
scenario_options: Production, because it has the most realistic data
UAT: the preproduction environment for validating changes before going live
Development, which is used for active feature work and unit tests
Ask the client to test it directly in their portal
nodes.scenario_explanation: UAT is the preproduction validation environment. Using Production would risk impacting live customers. Development is for developer unit testing, not prelaunch validation.

nodes.title: User & Access Management
nodes.description: Role based access control, user provisioning, and permission tiers in Fingen.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Fingen uses Role Based Access Control (RBAC) to govern which modules and actions each user can perform. Access issues are among the most common L2 tickets.

## Roles and Permissions
- **Admin**: Full read/write across all modules including Config Service
- **Operator**: Read/write for Accounts and Transactions; no Config access
- **Viewer**: Read only across Accounts, Transactions, and Reports
- **Support**: Read only for Accounts, Transactions, and Audit Logs (standard L2 role)

## User Provisioning Flow
1. Access request raised via the client's identity provider (Azure AD or Okta)
2. IdP syncs user to Fingen via POST /api/users/sync
3. Role assigned in Fingen Admin Panel
4. User receives first login email (link expires in 24 hours)

## Common L2 Issues
- **Cannot log in**: Check IdP account status first. Then verify Fingen sync: GET /api/users/{id}. Check status = ACTIVE.
- **Missing module access**: Compare user's role against the permission matrix. Raise an access change request if a role upgrade is needed.
- **Role mismatch after IdP update**: Force resync: POST /api/users/sync with force: true.

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT id, name, email, role, status, last_login
FROM users WHERE email = 'client@example.com';
```
nodes.sample_question: What is the first step an L2 engineer should take when a user reports they cannot log in to Fingen?
nodes.sample_answer: Check the user account status in the identity provider. Confirm whether the account is active, locked, or disabled. Then check the Fingen user sync status via GET /api/users/{id} to verify the account exists and has the correct role assigned.
nodes.scenario_context: A client operator reports they can log in but cannot access the Transaction module. Their Fingen role shows as 'Viewer'. What is the most likely cause?
scenario_options: Their browser cache needs clearing
The Transaction module may not be included in the Viewer role's permission set; verify it and raise an access change request if needed
The Production environment is down
The operator is using the wrong URL
nodes.scenario_explanation: RBAC defines which modules each role can access. Viewer is a read only role and may not include Transaction module access. Check the permission matrix before escalating.

nodes.title: Account Module
nodes.description: Account types, lifecycle states, and status codes in Fingen.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Account Module manages the full lifecycle of client accounts, from KYC and activation through to closure. Most transaction failures trace back to an account status issue.

## Account Statuses
- **PND**: Pending: KYC not yet complete; transactions blocked
- **ACT**: Active: fully operational
- **SUS**: Suspended: compliance or fraud hold; transactions blocked
- **CLO**: Closed: archived; all transactions rejected
- **REV**: Under Review: flagged for compliance investigation

## Account Types
- **CURRENT**: Standard operating account supporting debits and credits
- **SETTLEMENT**: Internal settlement account used by the Transaction Engine
- **VIRTUAL**: Subaccount linked to a parent; inherits parent limits unless overridden

## KYC Activation
New accounts start in PND. KYC documents are uploaded via the Web Portal. Once compliance approves, the account transitions to ACT automatically. If stuck in PND beyond 5 business days:

```sql
SELECT * FROM kyc_checks WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC;
```

## Common L2 Diagnostics
```sql
-- Check account status and compliance hold
SELECT status, compliance_hold, daily_limit FROM accounts WHERE account_number = 'ACC-XXXXXX';

-- Find who triggered a status change
SELECT ts, actor_type, action, old_value, new_value
FROM audit_log WHERE entity_type = 'ACCOUNT' AND entity_id = ?
ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 5;
```
nodes.sample_question: A client reports that their account is unexpectedly in SUS status. What steps would you take to investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Query the account via GET /api/accounts/{id} to confirm the status. Check the audit log for the suspension event to identify who or what triggered it. Escalate to the Account Operations team if the cause is unclear.
nodes.scenario_context: A client's Current account is in SUS status. The audit log shows the status changed at 02:14 UTC during a scheduled compliance run. The client says they made no unusual transactions. What is your next action?
scenario_options: Immediately reactivate the account to unblock the client
Ask the client to submit a formal complaint
Check which compliance rule triggered the suspension and escalate to the Account Operations team for review
Close the account and open a new one
nodes.scenario_explanation: Compliance triggered suspensions must be reviewed by Account Operations before any reactivation. Bypassing this process would be a compliance violation.

nodes.title: Transaction Engine
nodes.description: Transaction types, processing pipeline, and status transitions.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Transaction Engine processes every payment through a defined lifecycle. Understanding each status and transition rule lets you pinpoint exactly where a stuck transaction is blocked.

## Transaction Lifecycle
```
INITIATED → VALIDATED → AUTHORISED → PROCESSING → SETTLED
                ↓               ↓           ↓
           REJECTED        DECLINED     FAILED
```

## Status Definitions
- **INITIATED**: Received, not yet validated
- **VALIDATED**: Passed field/format checks; queued for authorisation
- **AUTHORISED**: Passed balance and limit checks
- **PROCESSING**: Sent to settlement engine; awaiting confirmation
- **SETTLED**: Final; funds moved successfully
- **REJECTED**: Failed validation (bad data, duplicate)
- **DECLINED**: Failed authorisation (insufficient funds, limit exceeded)
- **FAILED**: Error during settlement or downstream system fault

## Key Diagnostic Queries
```sql
-- Current status and detail
SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, status, error_code, created_at, updated_at
FROM transactions WHERE txn_id = 'TXN-XXXXXX';

-- Full status history
SELECT status, changed_at, changed_by, reason
FROM txn_status_log WHERE txn_id = 'TXN-XXXXXX' ORDER BY changed_at ASC;
```

## Common Stuck Transaction Causes
- Stuck in **PROCESSING** > 2 hrs: Settlement batch may have failed; check the batch_runs table
- Stuck in **AUTHORISED**: Transaction Service queue backlog; check the service logs
- Unexpected **FAILED**: Check txn_error_log for error_code and error_detail
nodes.sample_question: A transaction is stuck in PROCESSING status for over 30 minutes. What is your first action?
nodes.sample_answer: Check the transaction audit log to identify the last processing step completed. Determine if the issue is in authorisation, balance validation, or the downstream settlement service. Raise a P2 incident if the settlement service is unavailable.
nodes.scenario_context: Transaction TXN-8821 has been in PROCESSING status for 45 minutes. The Authorisation Service health check is passing. What should you check next?
scenario_options: Wait another 30 minutes, as transactions can take up to 2 hours
Manually update the transaction status to COMPLETED in the database
Check the settlement service health endpoint and review the transaction audit log for the last completed step
Reject the transaction and ask the client to resubmit
nodes.scenario_explanation: If Auth is healthy but the transaction is stuck, the bottleneck is likely downstream (settlement or GL). Reviewing the audit log pinpoints exactly where processing stalled.

nodes.title: Reporting Suite
nodes.description: Standard reports, scheduled delivery, and report parameter configuration.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Reporting Suite generates scheduled and on demand reports delivered to clients via SFTP, email, or API webhook. Report delivery failures are a frequent source of client complaints.

## Report Types
- **Transaction Summary**: Daily/weekly aggregation of all transactions by status
- **Settlement Confirmation**: Post settlement confirmation with net positions per currency
- **Reconciliation Report**: Breaks and matched items for a given date range
- **Audit Export**: Compliance grade export of all user actions and data changes
- **Custom Client Report**: Client specific format negotiated at onboarding

## Delivery Methods
- **SFTP**: Config: delivery_config.sftp_host / sftp_user. Fails: credential expiry, host key mismatch
- **Email**: Config: delivery_config.email_recipients. Fails: spam filter, invalid address
- **API Push (Webhook)**: Config: delivery_config.webhook_url. Fails: 4xx/5xx from client endpoint
- **Portal Download**: No delivery failure possible; access issues only

## Report Lifecycle
```
SCHEDULED → GENERATING → GENERATED → DELIVERING → DELIVERED
                              ↓              ↓
                         GEN_FAILED    DELIVERY_FAILED
```

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT report_id, report_type, scheduled_date, status, delivery_method, error_detail
FROM reports
WHERE status IN ('GEN_FAILED','DELIVERY_FAILED')
AND scheduled_date >= CURRENT_DATE - 7;
```

## L2 Action for DELIVERY_FAILED
1. Confirm the report was generated (status = GENERATED)
2. Check delivery_config for the account
3. For SFTP: test connectivity, check for expired credentials
4. Retry: POST /api/reports/{report_id}/retry
nodes.sample_question: A client says their Daily Transaction Summary report did not arrive this morning. How would you investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Check the REPORT_RUN table for the scheduled run. If FAILED, review the error description. Check the delivery destination configuration. If the run succeeded, investigate the delivery mechanism separately.
nodes.scenario_context: The client's Daily Transaction Summary shows FAILED in REPORT_RUN with error 'SFTP_AUTH_FAILURE'. What is your immediate action?
scenario_options: Rerun the report immediately without investigating
Check and update the SFTP delivery credentials in the report configuration, because expired or incorrect credentials cause SFTP_AUTH_FAILURE
Escalate to L3 engineering immediately
Notify the client the report will be 24 hours late
nodes.scenario_explanation: SFTP_AUTH_FAILURE is a credential error. Verify the SFTP username, password, and key are current before rerunning the report. Otherwise it will fail again.

nodes.title: Integration Layer
nodes.description: Third party integrations, webhook events, and API gateway usage.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Integration Layer connects Fingen to external systems. Client applications call in via the API Gateway, and Fingen pushes data out via webhooks and file exports. Integration failures can silently stop data flowing without a visible error.

## Inbound Integrations
- **REST API**: Client systems authenticate with X-API-Key header; all endpoints versioned under /api/v1/
- **File Upload (SFTP)**: Bulk payment and reference data files dropped to client specific SFTP directories
- **CBS Feed**: Automated inbound data from the client's Core Banking System every 15 minutes

## Outbound Integrations
- **Webhooks**: Event driven push to client HTTP endpoints for transaction status changes, report delivery, account events
- **SFTP Report Delivery**: Scheduled report files pushed to client SFTP
- **Downstream API Calls**: Calls to external clearing and settlement networks

## Webhook Event Types
TXN_STATUS_CHANGE | REPORT_DELIVERED | ACCOUNT_STATUS_CHANGE | BATCH_COMPLETE | SETTLEMENT_CONFIRMED

## Common L2 Issues
- **Webhooks not received**: Check webhook_delivery_log for HTTP status codes. 4xx usually means client endpoint config error; 5xx means client server error.
- **API key rejected**: Check api_keys table for expiry date and is_active flag
- **CBS feed stale**: Check data_ingestion_log for feed job status; stale > 1 hour triggers HIGH alert

## Webhook Retry Logic
Retries with exponential backoff: 1min → 5min → 15min → 1hr → 4hr. After max retries: status = ABANDONED. Manual retry: POST /api/integrations/webhooks/{event_id}/retry
nodes.sample_question: A downstream system reports it has stopped receiving webhook events from Fingen. What would you check?
nodes.sample_answer: Open the Gateway Console and filter for the downstream system's webhook endpoint. Check the delivery log for recent failures and HTTP response codes. Verify the endpoint URL is correct and the receiving system's firewall hasn't blocked Fingen's IP range.
nodes.scenario_context: The Gateway Console shows all webhook deliveries to the client's CBS are returning HTTP 403. All 3 retries are failing. What does this indicate?
scenario_options: The Fingen Integration Gateway is down
HTTP 403 (Forbidden) means the CBS endpoint is rejecting the requests, most likely because of an expired API key or token; check the integration authentication configuration
The CBS endpoint URL has changed, so update the DNS
Disable webhooks to CBS until it resolves itself
nodes.scenario_explanation: HTTP 403 is an authorisation failure at the receiving end, not a network issue. The CBS is reachable but rejecting Fingen's credentials. Check the API key or token expiry.

nodes.title: Data Dictionary
nodes.description: Core data entities, field definitions, code tables, and naming conventions.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Data Dictionary defines every key table and column in Fingen. L2 engineers need to know where data lives to run accurate triage queries.

## Core Tables Reference
| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| users | Fingen user accounts, roles, IdP sync status |
| accounts | Client accounts: status, type, limits |
| transactions | Every payment record with current status |
| txn_status_log | Immutable status transition history |
| batch_runs | Scheduled and ad hoc batch job records |
| reports | Report generation and delivery records |
| delivery_config | Per account delivery method configuration |
| webhook_delivery_log | All outbound webhook attempts and responses |
| audit_log | Immutable record of all user and system actions |
| kyc_checks | KYC document submission and approval status |
| config_params | Runtime config key value pairs per environment |
| data_ingestion_log | CBS and external feed ingestion job results |
| exception_queue | Payments requiring manual review |
| recon_breaks | Open reconciliation discrepancies |

## Key Relationships
- transactions.account_id → accounts.id
- txn_status_log.txn_id → transactions.txn_id
- reports.account_id → accounts.id
- audit_log.entity_id → any entity (check entity_type column)

## Read Only Reminder
L2 engineers have SELECT only access in Production. Any data modification requires an approved Change Request executed by L3 with DBA oversight. Never attempt UPDATE or DELETE on Production tables.
nodes.sample_question: You receive an API response with account_status: 'PND'. What does this mean and what action is typically required?
nodes.sample_answer: PND means Pending: the account is created but not yet fully activated. KYC verification or initial funding is still outstanding. The client needs to complete activation steps.
nodes.scenario_context: An API response returns 'acct_status': 'CLO' for an account the client believes is active. How do you interpret this and what do you do next?
scenario_options: The field name is incorrect, so ignore it and look elsewhere
CLO is an internal code that does not affect the client facing status
CLO means Closed per the Data Dictionary; verify in the audit log when and why the account was closed
The API must have a bug, so escalate to L3 immediately
nodes.scenario_explanation: CLO = Closed is defined in the ACCOUNT_STATUS code table. The audit log will show the closure event, actor, and timestamp to determine whether this was intentional.

nodes.title: Configuration Management
nodes.description: Environment configuration, feature flags, and system parameters.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Config Service manages runtime parameters controlling Fingen's behaviour: transaction limits, batch schedules, feature flags, and integration endpoints. Misconfiguration is a common root cause of limit related failures.

## Configuration Scopes
- **Global**: Applies to all accounts unless overridden (e.g. default daily limit)
- **Account level**: Per account overrides (e.g. higher limit for a premium client)
- **Environment level**: Separate values for Dev / UAT / Production

## Key Parameters for L2
| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| txn.daily_limit.default | Default daily transaction limit |
| txn.velocity.max_count_per_hour | Max transactions/hour before VELOCITY_BREACH |
| batch.settlement.cutoff_time | Daily settlement cutoff time (HH:MM UTC) |
| report.sftp.retry_attempts | SFTP delivery retry count |
| webhook.max_retries | Max webhook delivery attempts |
| dedup.window_seconds | Transaction dedup window (default: 60) |

## Retrieving Config
```
GET /api/config/{scope}/{key}
GET /api/config/account/{account_id}/{key}
```

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
-- Check account-level override for daily limit
SELECT value FROM config_params
WHERE scope = 'account' AND account_id = ? AND key = 'txn.daily_limit';
```

## Config Cache
The Config Service caches values for 5 minutes. After a config change, wait 5 minutes or call POST /api/config/cache/invalidate (requires Admin role) to force immediate refresh.
nodes.sample_question: A transaction limit for a client appears lower than agreed. Where would you check to verify the configured limit?
nodes.sample_answer: Use the Config Service read endpoint to retrieve the current transaction limit parameter for the relevant account type. Compare against the agreed limit in the client configuration document. Raise a Change Request if there is a discrepancy.
nodes.scenario_context: A client urgently needs their daily debit limit increased from £50,000 to £100,000 in Production before 09:00 tomorrow. What is the correct process?
scenario_options: Make the change directly in the Config Service to avoid delays
Raise a Standard Change Request and wait for the next CAB meeting in 3 days
Raise an Emergency Change Request, obtain verbal CAB approval, implement, and document everything same day
Ask an L3 engineer to make the change informally
nodes.scenario_explanation: Urgent Production config changes use the Emergency CR path: verbal CAB approval first, then change, then same day documentation. Bypassing change management is a compliance violation.

nodes.title: Audit Trail & Compliance
nodes.description: Audit logging, compliance checks, and regulatory report generation.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Every action in Fingen, whether by users, operators, or automated services, is written to the immutable audit log. For L2 engineers, the audit log is the primary source of truth for "who did what and when."

## What Is Logged
- User login and logout events
- Account status changes (who triggered it and the reason)
- Transaction state transitions (system generated)
- Configuration changes (key, old value, new value, changed by)
- Report generation and delivery attempts
- API key creation and revocation
- All Admin Panel actions

## Audit Log Query
```sql
SELECT event_id, ts, actor_type, actor_id, action,
       entity_type, entity_id, old_value, new_value, ip_address
FROM audit_log
WHERE entity_id = 'ACC-001234'
ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20;
```
actor_type is USER (human action) or SYSTEM (automated process).

## Compliance Requirements
- Audit logs are retained for **7 years** under financial services regulations
- Never attempt to delete or alter audit log records
- For client audit export requests: use the Audit Export report type and never provide raw database exports

## Common L2 Use Cases
- **Unexpected account suspension**: Search for action = 'STATUS_CHANGE' with entity_id = account_id
- **Prove a transaction was submitted**: Search action = 'TXN_CREATED' with entity_id = txn_id
- **Identify who changed a config value**: Search action = 'CONFIG_CHANGE' with entity_type = 'CONFIG'
- **Check if a user logged in during a suspicious window**: Search by actor_id = user_id across the date range
nodes.sample_question: How would you use the audit trail to confirm whether a specific user modified an account record yesterday?
nodes.sample_answer: Query AUDIT_EVENT filtering by resource_type=ACCOUNT, resource_id={account_id}, and timestamp within yesterday's date range. Filter by the suspected user's actor_id. Review event_type and before/after values.
nodes.scenario_context: You suspect a user modified a client account record at approximately 14:30 yesterday without authorisation. Where do you start the investigation?
scenario_options: Call the user directly and ask them
Query AUDIT_EVENT filtered by resource_type=ACCOUNT, the account's resource_id, timestamp 14:00 to 15:00 yesterday, and the suspected actor_id
Run a full database backup and search it
Check the users table for recent logins
nodes.scenario_explanation: AUDIT_EVENT is the authoritative, tamper evident record for all data changes. Filtering by resource, time, and actor gives a precise answer without invasive actions.

nodes.title: Platform Health & Monitoring
nodes.description: Health endpoints, operational dashboards, key metrics, and alert thresholds.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Platform Health monitoring is the L2 engineer's early warning system. Knowing which dashboards to check, which metrics matter, and which alert thresholds require escalation enables fast incident response.

## Operations Dashboard Panels
- **Service Health**: RED/AMBER/GREEN per microservice with current error rate %
- **Transaction Throughput**: Real time TPS vs baseline (alert if > 50% below baseline)
- **Settlement Queue Depth**: Transactions queued for settlement; spikes indicate batch delays
- **Report Delivery Rate**: % of scheduled reports delivered on time today
- **Integration Health**: Inbound API error rate and outbound webhook delivery rate
- **Alert Feed**: Active and recently resolved alerts with timestamps

## Key SLA Metrics
| Metric | SLA Threshold |
|---|---|
| Transaction processing P95 | < 3 seconds |
| Settlement batch completion | Within 2 hours of cutoff |
| Scheduled report delivery | Within 30 minutes of scheduled time |
| Platform API availability | 99.9% monthly uptime |

## Alert Severity Mapping
- **CRITICAL** → P1 incident immediately; wake on call engineer
- **HIGH** → P2; investigate within 30 minutes
- **MEDIUM** → Investigate within 4 hours
- **LOW** → Review during business hours

## Monitoring Tools for L2
- **Operations Dashboard** (Grafana based, read only): primary health view
- **PagerDuty**: on call alert routing and acknowledgement
- **Kibana** (index: fingen-prod-*): log search and error investigation
nodes.sample_question: The Operations Dashboard shows transaction FAILED rate at 5%. What are your immediate steps?
nodes.sample_answer: Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert. Check the error log for the most common failure reason code. Determine if failures are isolated to a specific type or integration endpoint. Raise a P2 incident if the cause cannot be identified within 15 minutes.
nodes.scenario_context: The Operations Dashboard shows API p95 latency at 1,200ms (threshold: 800ms). Transactions are completing successfully but slowly. How do you classify this?
scenario_options: No action, as latency is below the outage threshold
P1, because the platform is down
P2: major feature degradation; check infrastructure metrics and engage on call engineering
P4: low priority, address it the next business day
nodes.scenario_explanation: Latency above threshold with successful processing is degradation, not an outage, so it is P2. P1 requires platform wide failure. Checking infra metrics will reveal whether it's a DB, network, or service bottleneck.

nodes.title: Payment Initiation
nodes.description: How payments enter Fingen, channel types, and initial validation rules.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Payment initiation is the entry point for all transactions in Fingen. Every payment, whether from the web portal, a client API call, or a bulk file, passes through the same intake and validation pipeline before entering the processing queue.

## Initiation Channels
- **REST API**: Programmatic / real time single payments via POST /api/payments
- **Web Portal**: Manual entry by operators for individual payments
- **File Upload**: Bulk payment batches via CSV or JSON (SFTP or Portal upload)

## Validation Rules (applied to all channels)
1. **Field presence**: Mandatory fields: account_id, amount, currency, payment_ref
2. **Format validation**: Currency must be valid ISO 4217; amount must be numeric and positive
3. **Deduplication**: payment_ref checked against the last 60 seconds (configurable); duplicate → DUPLICATE_TXN
4. **Account existence**: Originating and beneficiary accounts must exist in ACT status

## Rejection Codes
| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| INVALID_ACCOUNT | Account not found or not in ACT status |
| DUPLICATE_TXN | Same payment_ref within dedup window |
| INVALID_CURRENCY | Currency code not supported |
| MISSING_FIELD | Mandatory field absent |
| LIMIT_EXCEEDED | Exceeds single transaction config limit |

## File Upload Investigation
```sql
SELECT file_id, filename, submitted_at, total_records,
       accepted, rejected, error_summary
FROM file_upload_log WHERE account_id = ?
ORDER BY submitted_at DESC LIMIT 5;
```
nodes.sample_question: A client reports that a bulk payment file was uploaded but no transactions appeared in the system. What do you investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Check the File Upload processing log for the submitted file. Review the validation errors. Common causes are malformed CSV headers, invalid account numbers, or amounts exceeding daily limits. Extract the error_code for each rejected record and share with the client.
nodes.scenario_context: A client uploads a bulk payment file with 500 records. 23 records are rejected with DUPLICATE_TXN. The client insists all 500 are new, unique payments. What is the most likely explanation?
scenario_options: Override the duplicate check, because the client is always right
The client probably submitted the same file twice within 60 seconds and the deduplication window caught the repeats; verify with the client and resubmit unique records only
The Fingen database has a corruption issue
Raise a P1 incident immediately
nodes.scenario_explanation: DUPLICATE_TXN within the 60 second deduplication window almost always indicates a double submission. Verify the submission timestamp log and coordinate with the client to confirm before resubmitting.

nodes.title: Authorisation & Limits
nodes.description: Authorisation checks, credit and debit limits, and decline code interpretation.
nodes.content:
## Overview
After validation, each payment enters the Authorisation Service which checks financial limits, balances, and velocity controls before allowing the payment to proceed to settlement.

## Authorisation Checks (in order)
1. Account status: originating account must be ACT with no compliance hold
2. Balance check (debits): available balance >= payment amount
3. Credit limit check (credit products): outstanding + payment <= credit limit
4. Single transaction limit: amount <= txn.single_limit config value
5. Daily limit: sum of today's AUTHORISED + PROCESSING + SETTLED + this payment <= daily limit
6. Velocity control: transaction count and amount within configured rolling window

## Decline Codes
| Code | Meaning | L2 Action |
|---|---|---|
| INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | Balance too low | Advise client to fund account |
| DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | Daily limit reached | Check if earlier transactions are still in PROCESSING counting against limit |
| VELOCITY_BREACH | Too many transactions in rolling window | Check velocity config; wait for window to reset |
| ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED | Account in SUS or REV status | Investigate suspension cause first |

## Diagnostic Queries
```sql
-- Check today's usage vs limit
SELECT SUM(amount) as today_total, COUNT(*) as today_count
FROM transactions
WHERE account_id = ? AND DATE(created_at) = CURRENT_DATE
AND status IN ('AUTHORISED','PROCESSING','SETTLED');

-- Velocity: last 1 hour
SELECT COUNT(*) as count_1hr, SUM(amount) as amount_1hr
FROM transactions
WHERE account_id = ? AND created_at >= DATETIME('now', '-1 hour')
AND status NOT IN ('REJECTED','DECLINED');
```
nodes.sample_question: A client receives DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED on what they claim is their first transaction today. How do you investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Query the transaction history for today to confirm whether earlier transactions have already processed. Check if the limit is set at the account or product level. Verify the configured limit via the Config Service. Check if a prior transaction is still in PROCESSING and being counted against today's limit.
nodes.scenario_context: A client's DEBIT payment is declined with VELOCITY_BREACH. The client says they have only made 5 transactions today. What is the most likely explanation?
scenario_options: The client is wrong, because velocity controls only count transactions above £10,000
Velocity controls can be configured to trigger on transaction count, total amount, or frequency within a rolling time window, so the limit may apply across a shorter window than a full day
Manually approve the transaction to unblock the client
The Authorisation Service has a bug, so escalate to L3
nodes.scenario_explanation: Velocity controls are highly configurable: they can trigger on count per hour, total amount per day, or frequency within a rolling window. The client's 5 daily transactions may still breach an hourly or amount based velocity rule.

nodes.title: Settlement Processing
nodes.description: Settlement cycles, netting, cutoff times, and settlement account management.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Settlement is the process of moving funds between accounts after authorisation. Fingen runs settlement in scheduled batch cycles and in real time for priority payments. Settlement failures hold funds and can trigger client SLA breaches.

## Settlement Types
- **Batch Settlement**: Runs at configured cutoff times (default: 11:00 and 17:00 UTC). Processes all AUTHORISED transactions since the previous cutoff.
- **Real time Settlement**: For payments flagged priority: high. Processed immediately after authorisation.

## Settlement Cycle
```
AUTHORISED → [cut-off reached] → PROCESSING → [clearing confirms] → SETTLED
                                      ↓
                                    FAILED (see txn_error_log)
```

## Batch Monitoring Query
```sql
SELECT batch_id, batch_type, scheduled_time, start_time, end_time,
       status, total_txns, settled_txns, failed_txns
FROM batch_runs
WHERE batch_type = 'SETTLEMENT' AND DATE(scheduled_time) = CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY scheduled_time;
```

## Common Settlement Issues
- **Batch not started at scheduled time**: Check if previous batch is still RUNNING (stuck > 30 min past schedule → escalate L3)
- **High FAILED count**: Pull txn_error_log for batch ID. CLEARING_TIMEOUT and NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE = external network issue → L3
- **Transaction stuck in PROCESSING > 2 hrs**: Likely missed the batch. Check batch completed without picking it up → escalate

## Escalation Triggers
Escalate to L3 if: batch fails to start, > 10% of transactions FAIL in a single batch, or SYSTEM_ERROR appears in the batch error log.
nodes.sample_question: A client submitted a payment at 15:45 UTC and it has not settled. When should it settle and why?
nodes.sample_answer: The 16:00 UTC batch cutoff is at 15:30 UTC. Since the payment was submitted at 15:45, it missed the 16:00 batch and will be included in the 22:00 UTC batch.
nodes.scenario_context: A client submits a payment at 21:55 UTC. They call at 23:30 UTC saying the recipient has not received funds. What do you tell them?
scenario_options: The payment was rejected, so ask the client to resubmit tomorrow
The 22:00 UTC batch cutoff was at 21:30 UTC, so the payment missed it and will be processed in the next available settlement window (12:00 UTC tomorrow)
Manually trigger settlement for this one payment
Mark the transaction as SETTLED immediately
nodes.scenario_explanation: 21:55 UTC is after the 21:30 cutoff (30 min before the 22:00 batch). The payment is valid and queued for the next batch. Inform the client of the expected settlement time.

nodes.title: Reconciliation Workflow
nodes.description: Daily reconciliation process, break identification, and resolution procedures.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Reconciliation ensures Fingen's internal records match clearing network and Core Banking System records. Reconciliation breaks can indicate missing funds or data integrity problems, and they are among the highest priority issues in financial operations.

## Reconciliation Types
- **Internal Recon**: transactions table vs txn_status_log; continuous (real time)
- **Settlement Recon**: Fingen settled records vs clearing network confirmation file; daily post settlement
- **GL Recon**: Transaction amounts vs General Ledger postings; daily EOD
- **Client Recon**: Fingen records vs client's own records; on request

## Break Categories
| Break Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| MISSING_INBOUND | Clearing network shows a receipt; Fingen has no record |
| MISSING_OUTBOUND | Fingen shows SETTLED; clearing network has no record |
| AMOUNT_MISMATCH | Both sides have the record but amounts differ |
| STATUS_MISMATCH | Status differs between Fingen and clearing network |

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT break_id, break_type, txn_id, fingen_amount,
       external_amount, detected_at, assigned_to
FROM recon_breaks
WHERE status = 'OPEN' AND detected_at >= CURRENT_DATE - 3
ORDER BY detected_at DESC;
```

## L2 Action on a Break
1. Verify it is not a timing issue (transactions near cutoff appear as breaks temporarily, so wait 30 min before acting)
2. Pull the clearing network reference from the recon_breaks record
3. If genuine: raise a P2 incident; escalate to Finance Operations and L3
4. Never manually adjust transaction amounts; that requires a formal journal entry via Finance Ops
nodes.sample_question: The reconciliation report shows a MISSING_OUTBOUND break for a transaction. What does this mean and what do you do?
nodes.sample_answer: MISSING_OUTBOUND means Fingen has a record of sending the transaction but the Payment Network has not confirmed settlement. Check the Integration Gateway log for the outbound instruction and the network portal. Escalate to Settlements if the network shows no record.
nodes.scenario_context: The overnight reconciliation report shows an AMOUNT_MISMATCH: Fingen records £12,500 settled but the Payment Network confirms £12,050. What is your action?
scenario_options: Update the Fingen transaction amount to match the network figure immediately
Mark the break as resolved, because small discrepancies are normal
Investigate both records: check the transaction audit log in Fingen and the Payment Network portal for the same reference, then escalate to the Settlements team
Raise a P4 ticket and address it next week
nodes.scenario_explanation: AMOUNT_MISMATCH requires cross system investigation before any adjustment. Do not modify amounts without Settlements team authorisation. This could be a fee calculation error, partial payment, or a network rounding issue.

nodes.title: GL Posting
nodes.description: General ledger integration, posting rules, and double entry accounting principles.
nodes.content:
## Overview
GL (General Ledger) Posting translates every settled financial transaction into accounting double entry records that feed the bank's core accounting system. A GL posting error means the transaction processed in Fingen but the accounting entry was not created, which is a serious compliance gap.

## How GL Posting Works
After a transaction reaches SETTLED status, the GL Posting Service creates two journal entries:
- **Debit entry**: Reduces the originating account balance in the GL
- **Credit entry**: Increases the beneficiary account balance in the GL

Both entries are sent to CBS via the Integration Gateway. CBS acknowledges and entries are marked GL_POSTED.

## GL Error Codes
| Code | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| GL_POSTING_ERROR | CBS rejected the entry (schema mismatch, invalid GL code) | Pull CBS error detail; raise with Finance Operations |
| CBS_TIMEOUT | CBS did not respond within timeout | Automated retry; if 3rd retry fails → P2 incident |
| INVALID_GL_CODE | Account GL code mapping missing or incorrect | Config fix by Finance Ops |
| DUPLICATE_GL_ENTRY | Retry posted same entry twice | Confirm with Finance Ops before any action |

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
-- Transactions settled but not GL posted
SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, settled_at, gl_status, gl_error_code
FROM transactions
WHERE status = 'SETTLED' AND gl_status != 'GL_POSTED'
AND settled_at >= DATETIME('now', '-24 hours');
```

## Critical Escalation Rule
GL errors must be escalated to Finance Operations within 1 hour of detection, because they affect the bank's balance sheet. Do not retry GL posting without Finance Ops approval.
nodes.sample_question: Several transactions completed successfully but the client's accounting team reports GL entries are missing. What do you check?
nodes.sample_answer: Query GL_POSTING_ERROR for the relevant transaction IDs and date. Review the error reason. Check the GL system health endpoint. If the GL was temporarily unavailable, transactions may need to be reposted manually via Finance Operations.
nodes.scenario_context: Five transactions for a new account type that went live today show GL_POSTING_ERROR with 'ACCOUNT_MAPPING_NOT_FOUND'. What is the likely cause and correct action?
scenario_options: Delete the transactions and ask the client to resubmit tomorrow
The new account type has no GL posting rule configured; raise a Change Request to add the mapping, then repost the affected transactions through Finance Operations
Modify the GL mapping directly in the production database
Escalate to the client's accounting team to fix their GL system
nodes.scenario_explanation: New account types need GL posting rules added via the approved change process. Once the mapping CR is approved and applied, Finance Operations can repost the failed transactions.

nodes.title: Batch Processing
nodes.description: Batch job schedules, monitoring, failure detection, and recovery procedures.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Batch processing handles high volume, time based operations: settlement cycles, report generation, reconciliation, and downstream delivery all run as scheduled batch jobs. L2 engineers need to quickly identify when a batch has failed and assess the downstream impact.

## Batch Job Types
| Job | Schedule | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SETTLEMENT | 11:00 and 17:00 UTC | Processes all AUTHORISED transactions |
| RECON | 02:00 UTC | Daily reconciliation against clearing network |
| REPORT_GENERATE | Varies per client | Generates scheduled reports |
| REPORT_DELIVER | 30 min after generation | Delivers reports to client channels |
| GL_POSTING_SWEEP | 03:00 UTC | Sweeps any missed GL posting entries |
| CBS_INGEST | Every 15 minutes | Ingests Core Banking System data |

## Batch Status Codes
SCHEDULED → RUNNING → COMPLETED | PARTIAL_COMPLETE | FAILED

- **PARTIAL_COMPLETE**: Batch finished but some records failed; check failed_txns count
- **FAILED**: Batch did not complete; downstream jobs may be blocked (REPORT_DELIVER depends on REPORT_GENERATE)

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT batch_type, status, total_txns, completed_txns, failed_txns,
       ROUND((completed_txns * 100.0 / total_txns), 1) as success_pct,
       scheduled_time, end_time
FROM batch_runs
WHERE DATE(scheduled_time) = CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY scheduled_time;
```

## Stuck Batch Protocol
If a batch has been RUNNING for > 2× its usual duration: escalate to L3. Never manually kill batch processes, as this can leave data in a partially committed state.
nodes.sample_question: The 22:00 UTC settlement batch is showing FAILED status. What is your immediate response?
nodes.sample_answer: Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert. Check BATCH_RUN for the failure reason. If due to a transient error, follow the settlement batch rerun runbook. If due to a data error or service outage, raise a P1 incident and escalate to Settlements and Engineering immediately.
nodes.scenario_context: The 22:00 UTC settlement batch shows FAILED in BATCH_RUN with error 'PAYMENT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT'. It is now 22:15 UTC. What is your first action?
scenario_options: Wait until morning to investigate, since settlement can catch up tomorrow
Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert, check Payment Network status, and follow the settlement batch rerun runbook if the network has recovered
Manually mark all pending transactions as SETTLED
Restart the database server
nodes.scenario_explanation: PAYMENT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT is transient: it means the network was temporarily unreachable. If the network has recovered, the rerun runbook lets you restart from checkpoint without reprocessing already settled transactions.

nodes.title: Real time vs Batch Flows
nodes.description: Operational differences, SLA requirements, and when each processing mode applies.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Not all operations in Fingen use the same processing model. Understanding when real time vs batch processing is used is essential for setting correct client expectations and diagnosing timing related issues.

## Real time Processing (Synchronous)
Used for: single payment authorisation, account status checks, webhook delivery for high priority events
- Response SLA: < 3 seconds (P95)
- Failure mode: immediate error response with error_code returned to caller
- Monitoring: Transaction Service error rate on Operations Dashboard

## Batch Processing (Asynchronous)
Used for: settlement cycles, report generation, reconciliation, GL posting, bulk file processing
- Failure mode: silent failure recorded in batch_runs, with no immediate client facing error
- Monitoring: Batch Jobs panel and alert feed

## Key Distinctions for L2 Triage
| Symptom | Likely Processing Type | Investigation Path |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate error on payment | Real time validation/auth failure | Check error_code in API response |
| Payment AUTHORISED but not SETTLED | Batch settlement issue | Check batch_runs for settlement batch |
| Report not received | Batch generation or delivery issue | Check batch_runs and reports table |
| All payments normal but GL not updated | GL_POSTING_SWEEP batch issue | Check batch_runs for GL_POSTING_SWEEP |

## Cutoff Time Impact
Payments submitted after the 17:00 UTC settlement cutoff will not settle until the next day's 11:00 batch. Always check submission timestamp vs cutoff before telling a client their payment "should have settled today."
nodes.sample_question: A client asks why their payment authorisation was instant but funds have not appeared in the recipient's account. How do you explain this?
nodes.sample_answer: Authorisation is real time and confirms the payment is approved and funds reserved. Actual fund delivery depends on the settlement batch, which runs at scheduled intervals. The funds will appear after the next batch cycle completes.
nodes.scenario_context: A client calls 20 minutes after an approved payment to say the recipient's bank shows no credit. They want to know if the payment went through. How do you explain this?
scenario_options: Tell the client the payment failed and ask them to try again

Authorisation was real time (instant confirmation) but the actual fund transfer depends on the next scheduled settlement batch. The recipient will receive funds after that batch completes, typically within a few hours
Escalate to P1, because funds are missing
Tell the client to wait 48 hours
nodes.scenario_explanation: Authorisation and settlement are separate flows. Real time authorisation means approved and reserved, not yet delivered. Settlement is the batch process that moves the funds. This is standard for batch settled payments.

nodes.title: Exception Handling
nodes.description: Exception queues, manual override procedures, and escalation triggers.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Exception Queue holds payments that could not be processed automatically due to data issues, authorisation edge cases, or downstream errors. Efficient exception queue management is a core daily task for L2 engineers.

## Exception Types
| Type | Cause |
|---|---|
| VALIDATION_EXCEPTION | Passed intake but failed deeper validation (e.g. account closed after submission) |
| SYSTEM_EXCEPTION | Infrastructure error during processing (e.g. DB timeout, CBS unavailable) |
| AUTHORISATION_EXCEPTION | Authorisation rule triggered requiring manual review |
| DUPLICATE_EXCEPTION | Suspected duplicate requiring human confirmation |

## Exception Queue Workflow
1. **Triage**: Review the exception; categorise by type and urgency
2. **Investigate**: Pull transaction detail and error_code from txn_error_log
3. **Action**: Approve (manual override after review), Reject (close with reason), Resubmit (fix data), or Escalate (L3 for SYSTEM_EXCEPTION)
4. **Document**: All exception actions must be logged in the incident ticket

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT e.exception_id, e.exception_type, t.txn_id, t.amount,
       e.error_code, e.error_detail, e.created_at
FROM exception_queue e
JOIN transactions t ON t.txn_id = e.txn_id
WHERE t.account_id = ? AND e.status = 'OPEN'
ORDER BY e.created_at ASC;
```

## SLAs
- VALIDATION_EXCEPTION: review within 4 hours
- SYSTEM_EXCEPTION: review within 1 hour (may indicate platform wide issue)
- AUTHORISATION_EXCEPTION: review within 2 hours

## Escalation Trigger
If SYSTEM_EXCEPTION volume spikes (> 10 new in 15 minutes): check for platform wide issue and raise P2 incident.
nodes.sample_question: You find 50 transactions in SYSTEM_EXCEPTION with error 'DOWNSTREAM_TIMEOUT'. What does this mean and what do you do?
nodes.sample_answer: DOWNSTREAM_TIMEOUT means processing attempted to call a downstream service and did not receive a response within the timeout window. Check the downstream service health. If it has recovered, use the exception resubmit runbook. Raise a P2 incident if more than 10 items are affected.
nodes.scenario_context: You notice 30 transactions in MANUAL_REVIEW status in the exception queue. A colleague suggests resolving them all quickly to clear the backlog. What do you do?
scenario_options: Agree and help clear the queue, because the client is waiting
MANUAL_REVIEW transactions are compliance holds. Only the Compliance team can action these. Never touch MANUAL_REVIEW items as a support engineer
Apply the SYSTEM_EXCEPTION resubmit runbook to all 30
Reject all 30 to clear the queue
nodes.scenario_explanation: MANUAL_REVIEW = compliance hold. These are flagged by the compliance engine and require Compliance team review. Support engineers touching these items would be a serious compliance violation.

nodes.title: Data Ingestion Pipeline
nodes.description: Source systems, ingestion schedules, transformation rules, and data quality checks.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Data Ingestion Pipeline receives data from the client's Core Banking System (CBS) and other upstream sources. It runs every 15 minutes and provides account balance updates and confirmation files. When ingestion fails, downstream processes can use stale data.

## Ingestion Sources
| Source | Data Type | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| CBS | Account balances, account status | Every 15 minutes |
| Clearing Network | Settlement confirmation files | Post settlement (twice daily) |
| Reference Data Feed | Currency rates, holiday calendars | Daily at 07:00 UTC |
| Client Reference Data | Account mapping overrides | On change events |

## Ingestion Pipeline Stages
```
Source → Ingestion Gateway → Validation → Transformation → Load → Confirmation
```

## Failure Points
- **Ingestion Gateway**: Network connectivity to CBS; check VPN tunnel status if CBS feed stops
- **Validation**: Schema changes in source data; shows as VALIDATION_ERROR in data_ingestion_log
- **Load**: DB constraint violation; usually a duplicate key from double submission

## Diagnostic Query
```sql
SELECT job_id, source, ingestion_type, started_at, completed_at,
       status, records_received, records_loaded, error_count, error_detail
FROM data_ingestion_log
WHERE started_at >= DATETIME('now', '-2 hours')
ORDER BY started_at DESC;
```

## Impact of Ingestion Failure
If CBS balance data is stale by > 1 hour: HIGH alert fires. Authorisation will use the last known balance, which risks unnecessary declines or overspending. Escalate to L3 immediately if CBS ingestion fails for > 30 minutes.
nodes.sample_question: The CBS account data ingestion has not run for 3 hours. What is the impact and how do you investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Account data in Fingen may be stale, showing incorrect balances or status for accounts updated in CBS. Check INGESTION_RUN for the CBS job status. Raise a P2 incident if down for more than 2 hours, as it affects authorisation accuracy.
nodes.scenario_context: INGESTION_RUN shows the CBS account data ingestion has failed 3 times in 6 hours with error 'CBS_CONNECTION_REFUSED'. What is the impact and your action?
scenario_options: This is minor, so continue monitoring and check again tomorrow

CONNECTION_REFUSED means CBS is not accepting connections, most likely because of a CBS outage or firewall change. Raise a P2 incident and contact the CBS team to check availability. The 6 hour data gap may be affecting authorisation decisions
Disable the ingestion job until the error stops
Manually copy account data from CBS to Fingen
nodes.scenario_explanation: CONNECTION_REFUSED is not a data error: it means the source system is unreachable. A 6 hour data gap for account balances is a P2 impact because authorisation decisions may be using stale data.

nodes.title: Downstream Delivery
nodes.description: Report delivery, file exports, downstream notifications, and delivery confirmation.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Downstream Delivery is the final step: pushing data out to clients via SFTP, webhooks, or API callbacks. Delivery failures are often invisible to the client until they notice missing data, making proactive monitoring critical.

## Delivery Channels
| Channel | Used For | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| SFTP | Scheduled report files, bulk exports | Automated retry; manual via POST /api/reports/{id}/retry |
| Webhook (HTTP POST) | Real time event notifications | Exponential backoff retries; manual retry via API |
| API Callback | Settlement confirmations to client systems | Same as webhook |
| Secure Email | Ad hoc reports and compliance exports | Manual resend only |

## Webhook Retry Logic
Backoff: 1min → 5min → 15min → 1hr → 4hr. After max retries: status = ABANDONED.
The client endpoint must respond with HTTP 200. Any other response (including 201, 204) is treated as failure unless the delivery config specifies otherwise.

## Diagnostic Queries
```sql
-- Failed webhook deliveries, last 24 hours
SELECT event_type, http_status, response_body, attempt_count, last_attempt_at, status
FROM webhook_delivery_log
WHERE account_id = ? AND status != 'DELIVERED'
AND last_attempt_at >= DATETIME('now', '-24 hours')
ORDER BY last_attempt_at DESC;

-- SFTP delivery failures
SELECT delivery_id, report_id, sftp_host, error_detail, attempt_count
FROM delivery_log WHERE account_id = ? AND status = 'FAILED'
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;
```

## Manual Retry
```
POST /api/deliveries/{delivery_id}/retry
POST /api/webhooks/{event_id}/retry
```
Both require Support role. Document retry action in the incident ticket.
nodes.sample_question: A client reports they did not receive their end of day settlement file via SFTP. How do you investigate?
nodes.sample_answer: Check DELIVERY_LOG for the client's settlement file delivery entry. Confirm the file was generated by checking REPORT_RUN. If generated and delivery FAILED, review the error. Common causes are incorrect SFTP credentials, server unavailability, or directory permission issues.
nodes.scenario_context: A client's settlement file delivery has failed all 3 retry attempts. DELIVERY_LOG shows 'SFTP_DIRECTORY_NOT_FOUND' on every attempt. What is the most likely cause and action?
scenario_options: Enable retries again and continue waiting
The target SFTP directory path in the delivery configuration is incorrect or has been deleted; verify the correct path with the client and raise a Change Request to update the delivery configuration
Escalate to L3 to rebuild the SFTP server
Email the file to the client manually
nodes.scenario_explanation: SFTP_DIRECTORY_NOT_FOUND means the configured destination path doesn't exist on the client's SFTP server. Verify the correct path with the client, then raise a CR to update the delivery configuration.

paths.title: L2 Support Operations
paths.description: Runbook execution, incident management, escalation procedures, and client communication for L2 engineers.

nodes.title: Support Tier Model
nodes.description: L1, L2, and L3 responsibilities, escalation criteria, and handoff procedures.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Fingen uses a three tier support model. Knowing exactly what each tier owns prevents both under escalation (L2 trying to fix what only L3 can) and over escalation (sending L3 a password reset).

## Tier Responsibilities
| Tier | Owns | Does Not Own |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | Password resets, known issue scripts, portal navigation, ticket creation | Application investigation, database queries, runbook execution |
| L2 | Application investigation, runbook execution, triage queries, client communication, escalation coordination | Code changes, infrastructure changes, direct Production DB writes |
| L3 | Root cause analysis, code level fixes, infrastructure changes, complex data corrections | Day to day ticket handling |

## Handoff Requirements

**L1 → L2 Handoff must include:**
- Transaction ID / Account ID
- Reported error message and timestamp
- Steps already taken by L1
- Client contact name and ticket number

**L2 → L3 Escalation must include:**
- Full investigation summary (what was checked, what was found)
- Error codes and relevant log extracts
- Current SLA status and time remaining
- Proposed root cause hypothesis

## Critical Boundary: Production Data
L2 engineers have read only access to Production. Any Production data change requires an approved Change Request and must be executed by L3 under DBA oversight. This boundary protects data integrity and maintains audit trail compliance.
nodes.sample_question: A transaction stuck in PROCESSING is escalated from L1 to L2. What information should L1 have captured before the handoff?
nodes.sample_answer: L1 should document the transaction ID, account number, reported issue, timestamp, and all steps already taken. L2 acknowledges the handoff, confirms the SLA clock, and begins investigation without asking the client to repeat information.
nodes.scenario_context: An L1 engineer has found a stuck transaction in the database and wants to write an UPDATE SQL statement to manually set its status to COMPLETED. What do you do?
scenario_options: Help them write the UPDATE statement, because the client is waiting

L1 engineers do not have database write access, and manually updating production data requires an approved Change Request. Redirect L1 to the Transaction Investigation Runbook and handle the escalation to L2 properly
Ask L3 to do the UPDATE instead, bypassing the change process
Approve it just this once as an exception
nodes.scenario_explanation: Direct production database writes require an approved Change Request regardless of urgency. L1 has read only access. The Transaction Investigation Runbook defines the correct path for stuck transactions.

nodes.title: Incident Classification
nodes.description: Severity levels P1 to P4, impact assessment, and initial triage framework.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Correct incident classification determines response speed, team engagement, and SLA compliance. Misclassifying a P1 as P2 wastes critical minutes. Overclassifying P3s as P1 dilutes real alerts.

## Severity Matrix
| Priority | Definition | Response SLA | Notifications Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Platform wide outage or data integrity breach | 15 minutes | Engineering Manager, Client Success Director |
| P2 | Major feature unavailable, multiple clients affected | 30 minutes | Engineering Lead, Client Success Manager |
| P3 | Noncritical feature degraded, single client | 4 hours | Assigned L2 owner, Client Contact |
| P4 | Cosmetic issue or low impact query | 1 business day | Ticket assignee only |

## Classification Decision Tree
1. Is any client unable to make payments? → At minimum P2; all clients affected → P1
2. Is there a data integrity concern (missing funds, wrong amounts)? → P1 regardless
3. Is a nonpayment feature unavailable for multiple clients? → P2
4. Is one client experiencing a nonpayment issue? → P3
5. Is this a UI bug or informational query? → P4

## Reclassification
If investigation reveals wider or narrower impact than initially classified: reclassify immediately, adjust the notification chain, and document the reason in the ticket.

## Common Misclassifications
- Transaction search broken → P2 (not P1, because payments are still processing)
- Report 2 days late for 1 client → P3 (not P2, because the impact is isolated)
- All settlement failed → P1 (not P2, because the financial impact is platform wide)
nodes.sample_question: The transaction search feature is returning no results for all users. What severity do you classify this as and why?
nodes.sample_answer: P2: a major feature is unavailable affecting multiple clients, but core transaction processing is still operational. Escalate to P1 only if transaction processing is also impacted.
nodes.scenario_context: At 09:05 AM, the Operations Dashboard shows transaction FAILED rate at 100%. No payments are processing for any clients. How do you classify this?
scenario_options: P3: monitor for 30 minutes before acting
P4, because it will probably resolve itself
P1: platform wide outage; engage the on call engineering team and notify the Engineering Manager and Client Success Director within 15 minutes
P2: wait for the 30 minute response window to complete
nodes.scenario_explanation: 100% failure rate across all clients is a platform wide outage, which is P1 by definition. P1 requires a 15 minute initial response, executive notification, and immediate engineering engagement.

nodes.title: Runbook Navigation
nodes.description: Locating, reading, and executing runbooks, version control, and change log review.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Runbook Library contains approved, version controlled operational procedures for all common L2 tasks. A runbook must always be the first reference point before improvising any solution. Improvised fixes in Production are a leading cause of incidents being extended or worsened.

## Runbook Structure
Every runbook follows a standard structure:
1. **Scope**: What issue this runbook addresses and its preconditions
2. **Steps**: Numbered, explicit actions with expected outputs at each step
3. **Decision Points**: If/then branches for different outcomes
4. **Escalation Triggers**: Exactly when to stop and escalate to L3
5. **Rollback**: What to do if a step produces an unexpected result
6. **Post actions**: Documentation and client communication required after completion

## How to Find the Right Runbook
- **By category**: Transactions | Account & User | Batch & Reporting | Integration | Incident Management
- **By error code**: Search the runbook title for the error code (e.g. SETTLEMENT_FAILED, DELIVERY_FAILED)
- **By incident type**: Classify the incident first, then navigate to the appropriate category

## Using Runbooks Correctly
- Always use the latest **Approved** version; never use a Draft or Deprecated version in Production
- If a step is unclear or produces an unexpected result: **stop and escalate to L3**. Do not improvise.
- After completing a runbook: update the incident ticket with the runbook ID, version, steps completed, and outcome.

## Suggesting Updates
If you find a gap or error in a runbook: raise a runbook change request with the Runbook Owner. Do not edit runbooks directly without going through the approval process.
nodes.sample_question: You need to resubmit failed settlement batch transactions and find two versions of the runbook. How do you decide which to use?
nodes.sample_answer: Always use the higher version number, provided it is marked Approved. Check the change log to understand what changed between versions. If ambiguous, confirm with your team lead before proceeding.
nodes.scenario_context: The KB shows Settlement Batch Rerun Runbook v1.2 (Approved, updated 3 months ago) and v1.3 (Draft, updated yesterday). Which do you use?
scenario_options: v1.3, because it is the newest and will have the latest steps
v1.2, because it is the Approved version. v1.3 is still Draft and must not be used in Production until formally approved
Use whichever is shorter to save time
Write your own procedure based on both versions
nodes.scenario_explanation: Only Approved runbooks should be used in Production. Draft versions have not been reviewed, validated, or approved. Using a Draft runbook in Production is a process violation.

nodes.title: Common Failure Scenarios
nodes.description: Top recurring issues, symptoms, root causes, and first response actions.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Certain failure patterns appear repeatedly across Fingen client accounts. Knowing the top failure scenarios and their typical causes enables faster triage and reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR).

## Top 10 Failure Patterns

**1. Transaction stuck in PROCESSING**
Settlement batch failed or missed. Check batch_runs for the settlement batch status on the transaction date.

**2. DELIVERY_FAILED report**
SFTP credential expired or client endpoint unreachable. Check delivery_config and test SFTP connectivity.

**3. All payments DECLINED with DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED**
A prior large transaction still in PROCESSING is counting against the daily limit. Check transactions table for PROCESSING records.

**4. Webhook events not received by client**
Client endpoint returning 4xx/5xx. Check webhook_delivery_log. Often a TLS certificate expiry on the client side.

**5. User cannot log in (not password related)**
IdP sync failure. Check users table sync status and trigger a resync via POST /api/users/sync.

**6. Account stuck in PND status**
KYC document pending review beyond SLA. Check kyc_checks table for the blocking step.

**7. Report has wrong date range**
delivery_config has an incorrect schedule offset. Review config and raise a change request.

**8. CBS ingestion stale > 1 hour**
VPN tunnel to CBS may be down. Alert L3 (network team). Do not attempt to fix network infrastructure as L2.

**9. Exception queue spike**
CBS data returned stale balances, causing cascade of AUTHORISATION_EXCEPTIONs. Fix ingestion first, then bulk resubmit exceptions.

**10. GL posting errors spike at month end**
CBS GL code mapping not updated for month end chart of accounts changes. Escalate to Finance Operations immediately.
nodes.sample_question: A report that normally arrives at 07:00 has not arrived by 09:00. Without looking at any systems yet, what are the three most likely causes?
nodes.sample_answer: 1) The report generation batch job failed or ran late. 2) The delivery attempt failed (SFTP error, wrong credentials, or full directory). 3) The report generated and delivered but landed in the wrong directory or under a different filename.
nodes.scenario_context: The client reports that no scheduled reports have arrived for 3 days. You have confirmed that all report batch jobs show COMPLETED status in REPORT_RUN. What is your next step?
scenario_options: Tell the client the reports were sent and are not your problem

The batches ran but delivery is failing. Check DELIVERY_LOG for all 3 days and verify the SFTP delivery credentials and target directory. Also ask the client to check alternative directories or filenames on their end
Rerun all 3 days of reports without investigating
Escalate to L3, because delivery is their responsibility
nodes.scenario_explanation: Reports completed but not received means the failure is in delivery, not generation. Check DELIVERY_LOG before rerunning anything. Rerunning is wasteful if the delivery configuration is still broken.

nodes.title: Database Queries for Triage
nodes.description: Read only query toolkit, safe SQL patterns, and data integrity guidelines.
nodes.content:
## Overview
L2 engineers have read only SELECT access to the Production database. These curated queries cover the most common triage scenarios. Always confirm you are connected to the correct environment before running any query.

## Environment Check (run first every session)
```sql
SELECT current_database(), current_setting('app.environment');
-- Must return: fingen_prod | production
```

## Transaction Investigation
```sql
-- Full transaction detail
SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, payment_ref,
       status, error_code, created_at, updated_at
FROM transactions WHERE txn_id = 'TXN-XXXXXX';

-- Complete status history
SELECT status, changed_at, changed_by, reason
FROM txn_status_log WHERE txn_id = 'TXN-XXXXXX' ORDER BY changed_at ASC;

-- All transactions for an account today
SELECT txn_id, amount, currency, status, created_at
FROM transactions
WHERE account_id = ? AND DATE(created_at) = CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY created_at DESC;
```

## Account Investigation
```sql
-- Account status and limits
SELECT id, account_number, status, account_type, compliance_hold, daily_limit
FROM accounts WHERE account_number = 'ACC-XXXXXX';

-- Recent audit events
SELECT ts, actor_type, action, old_value, new_value
FROM audit_log WHERE entity_type = 'ACCOUNT' AND entity_id = ?
ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 10;
```

## Batch and Report Health
```sql
-- Today's batch summary
SELECT batch_type, status, total_txns, failed_txns, scheduled_time, end_time
FROM batch_runs WHERE DATE(scheduled_time) = CURRENT_DATE ORDER BY scheduled_time;

-- Failed reports, last 7 days
SELECT report_id, report_type, account_id, scheduled_date, status, error_detail
FROM reports WHERE status = 'DELIVERY_FAILED' AND scheduled_date >= CURRENT_DATE - 7;
```
nodes.sample_question: You need to find all FAILED transactions for account 12345 in the last 24 hours. Write a safe query and explain your safeguards.
nodes.sample_answer: SELECT txn_id, txn_type, amount, status, created_at FROM transactions WHERE account_id = 12345 AND status = 'FAILED' AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours' FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY; Safeguards: SELECT only, scoped WHERE clause, FETCH FIRST cap.
nodes.scenario_context: You need to find all FAILED transactions for account 99001 from yesterday. Which query is correct and safe for Production use?
scenario_options: SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE account_id = 99001
UPDATE transactions SET status='COMPLETED' WHERE account_id = 99001 AND status='FAILED'
SELECT txn_id, status, amount, created_at FROM transactions WHERE account_id = 99001 AND status = 'FAILED' AND created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - 1 FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY
DELETE FROM transactions WHERE status='FAILED'
nodes.scenario_explanation: Option C: SELECT only (no data modification), scoped WHERE clause (specific account + date + status), FETCH FIRST to prevent runaway results. Options B and D are write operations, which are strictly prohibited for L2 engineers.

nodes.title: Escalation Matrix
nodes.description: Who to escalate to, when, contact structure, and SLA breach protocols.
nodes.content:
## Overview
The Escalation Matrix defines exactly who to contact and when based on incident severity and the affected service area. Following the matrix ensures the right people are engaged at the right time.

## Escalation by Severity
| Severity | First Contact | If No Response in 15 min | Executive Notification |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | On call L3 Engineer (PagerDuty) | Engineering Manager + Client Success Director | CTO after 30 min unresolved |
| P2 | Engineering Lead (Slack #incidents) | Engineering Manager after 30 min | Client Success Manager after 1 hr |
| P3 | L3 ticket queue | Engineering Lead after 3 hrs | None unless client requested |
| P4 | L3 ticket queue | Engineering Lead next business day | None |

## Escalation by Service Area
| Service | L3 Owner | PagerDuty Rotation |
|---|---|---|
| Transaction Engine | Payments Engineering | fingen-payments-oncall |
| Settlement / GL | Finance Tech Engineering | fingen-finance-oncall |
| Reporting / Delivery | Data Platform Engineering | fingen-data-oncall |
| Integration / CBS | Integration Engineering | fingen-integration-oncall |
| Account / User | Platform Engineering | fingen-platform-oncall |

## Client Escalation Rule
During P1/P2 incidents, the Client Success Manager (CSM) manages all external communication. L2 engineers provide updates to the CSM and do not contact the client directly during an active P1/P2.

## Antipatterns to Avoid
- Escalating without a full investigation summary
- Waiting past the SLA trigger time hoping the issue resolves itself
- Contacting executives directly without going through the CSM
nodes.sample_question: You have been investigating a P2 transaction processing issue for 25 minutes without resolution. What should you have done 5 minutes ago?
nodes.sample_answer: At the 20 minute mark, an escalation to Payments Engineering on call should have been initiated via PagerDuty. The client should also have received a status update with a revised ETA.
nodes.scenario_context: It is 14:28. A P2 transaction processing issue was raised at 14:00. You have been investigating for 28 minutes and are very close to identifying the cause, but have not yet escalated. What should you do right now?
scenario_options: Continue, because you are almost at the answer and can escalate after resolving
Escalate immediately to Payments Engineering on call via PagerDuty and notify the client. You should have done this at the 20 minute mark. Do both now, even though you are close to resolving it
Downgrade to P3 to buy more investigation time
Wait for the 30 minute SLA to expire before escalating
nodes.scenario_explanation: P2 escalation to on call must happen at 20 minutes regardless of investigation progress. Being close to a solution does not waive the escalation requirement. Notify the client simultaneously.

nodes.title: Change Management
nodes.description: Change request process, CAB approvals, implementation steps, and rollback procedures.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Change Management controls how modifications to the Production environment are planned, approved, and executed. Every Production change, no matter how minor, must go through this process. The CAB exists to prevent outages caused by uncontrolled changes.

## Change Types
| Type | Definition | Approval | Lead Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | Preapproved, low risk change from approved template | Auto approved | Raise 24 hrs before |
| Normal | Planned change requiring CAB review | Weekly CAB vote | Raise 5 business days before |
| Emergency | Urgent change needed for P1/P2 resolution | Engineering Manager + On call Lead | Immediate; post approval < 1 hr |

## L2 Engineer Role in Change Management
L2 engineers do not execute changes directly in Production. The L2 role is to:
1. Identify that a change is required (e.g. a config parameter needs updating)
2. Document the required change with full justification in a Change Request (CR)
3. Work with the Change Manager to classify it (Standard/Normal/Emergency)
4. Provide technical context for the CAB or approver
5. Validate the outcome after L3 executes it

## Change Windows
- **Standard**: Tuesday and Thursday, 22:00 to 02:00 UTC
- **Emergency**: Any time with Engineering Manager approval; client notification required if > 15 min expected impact

## Post Change Validation
After every Production change: monitor the Operations Dashboard for 30 minutes. If new alerts appear within this window, immediately flag to the Change implementer for potential rollback.
nodes.sample_question: A client is urgently requesting a transaction limit increase in Production. How do you handle this?
nodes.sample_answer: Raise an Emergency Change Request with the justification, current and requested limit values, impact assessment, and rollback plan. Obtain verbal CAB approval and document it same day. Do not make the change without an approved CR.
nodes.scenario_context: You discover a misconfigured fee rate is charging clients 2% instead of the agreed 0.5%. You have identified the exact Config Service parameter. What is the correct action?
scenario_options: Fix it immediately, because clients are being overcharged and every minute costs them money
Raise a Normal Change Request and wait 48 hours for CAB approval
Raise an Emergency Change Request citing active client harm, obtain verbal CAB approval, correct the config, and document everything same day
Ask a colleague to make the change so you are not accountable
nodes.scenario_explanation: Active client financial harm justifies the Emergency CR path. Verbal CAB approval is required before the change. Fixing it without any CR, even to stop an overcharge, is a compliance violation that could cause bigger problems.

nodes.title: Monitoring & Alert Runbooks
nodes.description: Alert interpretation, dashboards, false positive identification, and response procedures.
nodes.content:
## Overview
Monitoring alerts are the proactive side of L2 support: they flag issues before a client calls. Every Fingen alert maps to a runbook. Knowing the common alerts and their runbooks dramatically reduces response time.

## Alert to Runbook Mapping
| Alert | Severity | Runbook |
|---|---|---|
| TXN_FAILURE_RATE_HIGH | HIGH/CRITICAL | Transaction Investigation & Resubmit |
| SETTLEMENT_BATCH_DELAYED | HIGH | Settlement Batch Rerun |
| SETTLEMENT_BATCH_FAILED | CRITICAL | Settlement Batch Rerun |
| EXCEPTION_QUEUE_SPIKE | HIGH | Exception Queue Management |
| RECON_BREAKS_DETECTED | HIGH | Reconciliation Break Investigation |
| REPORT_DELIVERY_FAILED | MEDIUM | Report Delivery Failure Investigation |
| SFTP_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRY_7D | LOW | SFTP Credential Renewal |
| CBS_INGESTION_STALE | HIGH | CBS Ingestion Failure Response |
| WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_ABANDONED | MEDIUM | Integration Gateway Diagnostic |
| GL_POSTING_ERRORS | HIGH | GL Posting Error Recovery |

## Alert Response Procedure
1. **Acknowledge** the alert in PagerDuty within the SLA window (stops the escalation chain)
2. **Verify** on the Operations Dashboard: confirm the alert is genuine (rule out false positives from monitoring restarts)
3. **Open** the associated runbook in the Runbook Library
4. **Execute** the runbook; document each step in the incident ticket

## False Positive Recognition
Some alerts fire during planned maintenance or immediately after a deployment. Check the Change Register for any changes in the last 30 minutes before treating an alert as a genuine incident.
nodes.sample_question: You receive a HIGH_FAILED_TXN_RATE alert at 02:00 UTC. A maintenance window is scheduled for 01:00 to 03:00 UTC. What do you do?
nodes.sample_answer: Check whether the maintenance activity could explain the elevated failure rate. If consistent with the maintenance scope, acknowledge and monitor for recovery. If higher than expected, raise an incident and escalate to the team performing the maintenance.
nodes.scenario_context: A SETTLEMENT_BATCH_FAILURE alert fires at 02:05 UTC. The maintenance schedule shows a planned database patching window from 01:30 to 02:30 UTC that includes the settlement service. What is your response?
scenario_options: Raise a P1 incident immediately, because settlement has failed

The alert is likely a false positive from the planned maintenance. Acknowledge it, check the maintenance team's latest status, and monitor for recovery after 02:30 UTC. Only raise an incident if the batch does not recover once the maintenance window closes
Ignore the alert and go back to sleep
Page the Engineering Director immediately
nodes.scenario_explanation: Maintenance windows can trigger infrastructure alerts. Confirm with the maintenance team whether this is expected before raising an incident. Acknowledge the alert (don't ignore it), and verify recovery after the window closes.

nodes.title: Client Communication Standards
nodes.description: Status update templates, escalation language, SLA reporting, and professional communication norms.
nodes.content:
## Overview
During incidents, client communication is as important as technical resolution. Poor communication causes client escalations and SLA disputes, even when the technical issue was resolved quickly.

## Communication Principles
